example_summary: Compensation of ₹ 5 lacs paid by Government of Chattisgarh to parents of Amit for Dantewada blast is fully exempt under Section 10(10BC).
source_provision:
### Section 10(10BC): Exemption of Disaster Compensation

| Statutory Element | Statutory Requirement | Legal Consequence |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Eligible Payer** | Central Government, State Government, or Local Authority | Exemption Applicable |
| **Eligible Recipient** | Individual assessee or Legal Heir of the individual | Exemption Applicable |
| **Trigger Event** | Disaster as defined u/s 2(d) of Disaster Management Act, 2005 | Full Tax Immunity |
| **Statutory Proviso** | Loss/damage previously allowed as a tax deduction | Exemption Denied to that extent |


#### Core Statutory Requirements

* **Definition of Disaster:** Any catastrophe, mishap, calamity, or grave occurrence arising from natural or man-made causes, or by accident/negligence, causing substantial loss of life, human suffering, or property damage beyond community coping capacity.
* **Payer Restriction:** Compensation paid by private entities, employers, or non-governmental organizations does **not** qualify for exemption under Section 10(10BC).


> [!WARNING] Statutory Proviso Exception: If the assessee has already claimed a deduction under the Income-tax Act for any loss or damage caused by the disaster, the compensation received to the extent of such claimed deduction shall **not** be exempt and will be chargeable to tax.

director.justification: The issue hinges on meeting specific statutory conditions under Section 10(10BC) to grant full tax exemption on compensation received by legal heirs.
director.visual_metaphor: A statutory gatekeeper shield verifying government source, disaster qualification, and legal heir status before granting full income tax immunity.
